title: Importer.apply never restores document.preferences, silently reverting every account-level preference to its default on export/import

description: Discovered during the 6a completeness sweep's export/import round-trip test (Packages/LillistCore/Tests/LillistCoreTests/Export/ExportImportRoundTripEqualityTests.swift): Importer.apply never touched document.preferences at all (Packages/LillistCore/Sources/LillistCore/Export/Importer.swift) -- an export -> wipe -> import cycle (manual export/import in Settings, and DataStoreResetService.resetAndReseedFromThisDevice) silently reverted trashRetentionDays, morningSummary*, defaultAllDay*, defaultTaskListSort, and defaultTagTintHex to their hardcoded defaults, discarding the user's real settings. Not one of the original 70 review findings -- a genuinely new defect surfaced by 6a's own completeness proof. Fixed in the same session: new Importer.applyPreferences(_:policy:ctx:) writes the document's PreferencesDTO into the destination's singleton AppPreferences row (creating it if absent), following Series/Tag's established 'incoming wins' precedent for .replaceExisting/.recencyWins (AppPreferences carries no modifiedAt); .skipExisting only skips when a row already exists to skip. ImportSummary gained a preferencesApplied: Bool field. Regression tests: ExportImportRoundTripEqualityTests (the completeness proof that caught it) plus three focused ImporterTests cases (fresh-store restore, skipExisting-leaves-existing-alone, skipExisting-still-populates-an-absent-row).
